articles.title: This former lawyer writes inclusive children’s books so kids of different abilities can enjoy the same stories
articles.content: “I had a deep yearning to fulfil other life aspirations,” Lee said. Lee had been writing as a hobby while in legal practice. She volunteered with National Parks Board (NParks), taking photos and writing about Singapore’s parks. While on sabbatical, she had lunch with her friend Hidayah Amin, founder of Helang Books, a local independent publishing house. Lee asked her: Why don’t bookstores in Singapore carry books for persons with vision loss?. Lee didn’t have any personal connection with visually impaired people
